title: Addon-Vitest: Add channel API to programmatically trigger test runs
body:
Works on https://github.com/storybookjs/mcp/issues/138

Companion PR: https://github.com/storybookjs/mcp/pull/131

<!-- If your PR is related to an issue, provide the number(s) above; if it resolves multiple issues, be sure to break them up (e.g. "closes #1000, closes #1001"). -->

<!--

Thank you for contributing to Storybook! Please submit all PRs to the `next` branch unless they are specific to the current release. Storybook maintainers cherry-pick bug and documentation fixes into the `main` branch as part of the release process, so you shouldn't need to worry about this. For additional guidance: https://storybook.js.org/docs/contribute

-->

## What I did

Added a new programmatic trigger to `addon-vitest`, which allows external actors (like addon-mcp) to trigger a test run and get results back via events on the channel.

To support this, I had to make additional modifications:

1. Add the channel to the `options`, so that any preset property (like `experimental_devServer`) automatically has access to the channel and can do stuff with it.
2. Replaced the flow for how addon-vitest gets the index on the server.
 
Previously, it would _fetch_ the `index.json` when necessary; however, it wouldn't know which origin/url to fetch from. To know that, the manager would send the origin to the server (`indexUrl`) on startup, because the client _does_ know where to fetch the index from. If this sounds bad, it's because it was, but it was a good compromise at the time.

But not anymore, because now you can trigger tests without even opening the manager UI once, which would leave `indexUrl` undefined, and crash the test run. So now it does the more clear thing, which is possible as of recently, but wasn't before. Now `addon-vitest` gets the index directly from `StoryIndexGenerator` on the server, and subscribes to changes to the index, so that when tests are triggered, the index is already available and up-to-date.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Potential undefined entries when story IDs don't exist in the index.**

When `requestStoryIds` is provided, the map operation on line 224 will return `undefined` for any ID that doesn't exist in `index.entries`. The cast to `StoryIndexEntry[]` masks this issue, potentially causing runtime errors when downstream code accesses properties on these undefined entries.

Consider filtering out undefined entries:


<details>
<summary>🛡️ Proposed fix to handle missing entries</summary>

```diff
 private getStories(requestStoryIds?: string[]): StoryIndexEntry[] {
   const index = this.testManager.store.getState().index;
   if (requestStoryIds) {
-    return requestStoryIds.map((id) => index.entries[id]) as StoryIndexEntry[];
+    return requestStoryIds
+      .map((id) => index.entries[id])
+      .filter((entry): entry is StoryIndexEntry => entry !== undefined);
   }
   return Object.values(index.entries).filter((entry) => entry.type === 'story');
 }
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/addons/vitest/src/node/vitest-manager.ts` around lines 221 - 227,
getStories may return undefined items when requestStoryIds contains IDs not
present in this.testManager.store.getState().index.entries; change the mapping
logic in getStories to skip missing entries (e.g., map then filter out undefined
or use flatMap to only include found StoryIndexEntry) so the returned array
contains only StoryIndexEntry objects and not undefined values. Update the code
path that uses getStories to rely on the cleaned array but do not rely on the
previous cast to StoryIndexEntry[] to hide missing entries. Ensure you reference
the getStories method and the index.entries lookup when making the fix.
```

</details>

comments.author: JReinhold
comments.body:
I'm not a huge fan of these type fixes, that are now necessary becauseo of the new Channel in options. If you have better solutions @kasperpeulen, please let me know.

Here's a summary of the issue:

---

## Root issue

- The failing `core` type checks were caused by a **TypeScript type identity mismatch**, not a runtime bug.
- Two different `Channel` declarations were being mixed in the same typed flows:
  - one from internal/source typing
  - one from generated `dist` typing
- `Channel` has a private field (`sender`), so TypeScript treats them as nominally incompatible even when they look structurally similar.
- That produced errors like:  
  `Type '...Channel' is not assignable to type 'Channel'` and  
  `Types have separate declarations of a private property 'sender'`.

## Why this fix was necessary

- Critical paths (`loadAllPresets`, `Options` objects, telemetry `presetOptions`) require a **single consistent channel type**.
- Without normalization at those boundaries, `nx check core -c production` fails even though runtime behavior is fine.
- The fix aligned typing at boundaries and used explicit boundary casts where TS could not infer safe overlap.
- This was necessary to:
  - remove false-positive type failures,
  - preserve existing runtime behavior,
  - keep CI (`core:check:production`) green.

## What changed (high level)

- Normalized `channel` typing at `loadAllPresets` / `Options` boundaries in core server build/load flows.
- Normalized telemetry `presetOptions` typing in the error-reporting/telemetry call sites.
- No intended behavior changes at runtime; this is a type-system consistency fix.

## Outcome

- `npx nx check core -c production --outputStyle=stream` now passes.
- The fix resolves the private-field `Channel` incompatibility errors that were blocking CI/type-check.

comments.author: kasperpeulen
comments.body:
The root cause is that `Channel` has a `private sender` field, so TypeScript treats the source-level and dist-level declarations as nominally incompatible even though they're structurally identical.

I tried `protected` — same issue ("Property 'sender' is protected but type 'Channel' is not a class derived from 'Channel'").

But adding `ChannelLike` interface works. I tested this locally. This makes sure we use structural typing instead of nominal everywhere.
